items.title: [Right coronary artery to right atrium fistula treated by percutaneous closure].
items.abstract: Coronary fistulas are rare congenital anomalies defined by an abnormal communication between a coronary artery and a cardiac chamber or great vessel. We report the case of a 5-year-old male patient (17 kg) referred for cardiac catheterization due to echocardiographic suspicion of patent ductus arteriosus. Coronary angiography revealed a fistula originating from the right coronary artery with direct drainage into the right atrium. Percutaneous closure was successfully performed using a COMED PDA 4/6 device. Post-procedural angiography showed complete occlusion without residual shunt. This case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic role of cardiac catheterization in congenital coronary anomalies. Las fístulas coronarias son anomalías congénitas poco frecuentes, caracterizadas por una comunicación anómala entre una arteria coronaria y una cavidad cardiaca o un gran vaso. Se presenta el caso de un paciente de 5 años (17 kg) remitido para cateterismo cardiaco ante la sospecha ecocardiográfica de persistencia del conducto arterioso. Durante el estudio angiográfico se identificó una fístula originada en la arteria coronaria derecha con drenaje directo a la aurícula derecha. Se realizó cierre percutáneo exitoso mediante dispositivo COMED PDA 4/6. El control angiográfico posterior mostró oclusión completa sin cortocircuito residual. Este caso resalta la utilidad del cateterismo cardiaco no solo para la caracterización anatómica precisa, sino también como herramienta terapéutica en anomalías coronarias congénitas en población pediátrica.

items.title: Retrospective Mexican experience in the transcatheter closure of atrial septal defects using different devices.
items.abstract: Over the past decades, significant advancements and innovations have occurred in the field of percutaneous atrial septal defect (ASD) closure using transcatheter-based devices. The Amplatzer septal occluder has been widely used since its Food and Drug Administration approval in 2001. Studies have shown its high success rate in closing ASDs. Since then, many other devices have been developed and used with high technical success and closure rates, with low rates of serious adverse events and device-related complications. When compared to surgery, percutaneous closure provides a less invasive approach with quicker recovery and reduced physical and psychological impact. To demonstrate the effectiveness of using different devices for transcatheter ASD closure, emphasizing the success and complications obtained in our patients. Patients with congenital ASDs who underwent transcatheter closure using different devices were included. The primary endpoint was to determine the efficacy and safety of these devices and to determine the incidence of complications at follow-up. Two hundred and eighty-seven patients underwent ASD closure at a median age of 6 years (7 months-70 years). Only minor complications occurred during catheterization. After a follow-up of 90 ± 67.7 months (up to 96 months), the closure rate was 98.6%, and the absence of atrioventricular block was 100%. Transcatheter ASD closure using percutaneous devices has proven to be safe and effective in most cases. However, careful patient selection and follow-up are necessary to minimize complications and ensure optimal outcomes. En las últimas décadas se han producido avances e innovaciones significativas en el cierre percutáneo de la comunicación interauricular (CIA) mediante dispositivos transcatéter. El oclusor septal Amplatzer (ASO) se ha utilizado ampliamente desde su aprobación por la FDA en 2001. Diversos estudios han demostrado su alta tasa de éxito en el cierre de la CIA. Desde entonces, se han desarrollado y utilizado muchos otros dispositivos con altas tasas de éxito técnico y de cierre, y con bajas tasas de eventos adversos graves y de complicaciones relacionadas con el dispositivo. En comparación con la cirugía, el cierre percutáneo ofrece un enfoque menos invasivo, con una recuperación más rápida y un menor impacto físico y psicológico. Demostrar la eficacia del uso de diferentes dispositivos para el cierre transcatéter de la CIA, destacando el éxito y las complicaciones obtenidas en nuestros pacientes. Se incluyeron pacientes con CIA congénita sometidos a cierre transcatéter con diferentes dispositivos. El objetivo principal fue determinar la eficacia y la seguridad de estos dispositivos, así como la incidencia de complicaciones durante el seguimiento. Se sometieron a cierre de CIA 287 pacientes, con una mediana de edad de 6 años (7 meses a 70 años). Durante el cateterismo solo se presentaron complicaciones menores. Tras un seguimiento de 90 ± 67.7 meses (hasta 96 meses), la tasa de cierre fue del 98.6% y la ausencia de bloqueo auriculoventricular fue del 100%. El cierre transcatéter de CIA mediante dispositivos percutáneos ha demostrado ser seguro y eficaz en la mayoría de los casos. Sin embargo, es necesario realizar una cuidadosa selección y un adecuado seguimiento de los pacientes para minimizar las complicaciones y garantizar unos resultados óptimos.

items.title: Sinus rhythm with persistent left atrial appendage tachycardia.
Tricuspid inflow E-wave velocity for the assessment of severe or greater tricuspid regurgitation: derivation and external validation of threshold values.
items.abstract: Current guidelines include tricuspid inflow E-wave (>100 cm/s by pulsed-wave Doppler) as a semiquantitative criterion for diagnosing severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR), despite limited supporting evidence. We assessed its diagnostic performance for identifying severe or greater TR, deriving and externally validating practical thresholds. Tricuspid inflow E-wave velocity was measured by pulsed-wave Doppler in consecutive patients with at least mild TR between December 2024 and February 2026. Among 178 patients (77±13 years, 65% women), TR was mild in 44, moderate in 61, severe in 44, massive in 15, and torrential in 14. Mean tricuspid E-wave velocity was 56±16 cm/s and increased with TR severity: 47±8, 50±10, 62±16, 67±13, and 77±21 cm/s for mild, moderate, severe, massive, and torrential TR. Only three patients had E-wave velocity >100 cm/s (one with severe and two with torrential TR). Using multiparametric echocardiographic grading as the reference standard, the >100 cm/s threshold showed 5.5% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and kappa 0.25 for severe or greater TR. As a continuous variable, E-wave velocity discriminated severe or greater TR with an AUC of 0.81. A lower threshold of 52 cm/s yielded 81% sensitivity and 67% specificity, whereas 47 cm/s provided 90% sensitivity and 43% specificity. External validation resulted in 94% sensitivity and 47% specificity. The guideline-recommended threshold of >100 cm/s is highly insensitive for detecting severe or greater TR. Lower cut-offs, particularly 47 cm/s, may be useful for screening to trigger a comprehensive multiparametric assessment.

items.title: Chronic kidney disease in heart failure: results from an Ecuadorian registry.
items.abstract: Heart failure (HF) frequently coexists with chronic kidney disease (CKD), a combination that is associated with worse outcomes. Data from Ecuador remain limited. We estimated the prevalence of CKD among patients with HF and described prognostic impact according to left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). A retrospective study was conducted using a single-center HF registry in Ecuador. CKD was defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 60 mL/min/1.73m2. HF was categorized by LVEF into reduced (HF with reduced ejection fraction [HFrEF], ≤ 40%), mildly reduced (HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction [HFmrEF], 41-49%), and preserved (HF with preserved ejection fraction [HFpEF], ≥ 50%). The median follow-up was 2.28 years. Among 706 patients (age 69.9 ± 13.3 years; 31.4% women), 50.3% had an eGFR ≥ 60, 33.1% had an eGFR of 30-59, and 16.6% had an eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2. CKD prevalence was 57.8% in HFrEF, 41.8% in HFmrEF, and 53.5% in HFpEF (p = 0.003). CKD patients were older and had higher rates of hypertension (HT), atrial fibrillation, and cerebrovascular disease, with higher NT-proBNP levels, larger diastolic diameters, lower LVEF, more tricuspid regurgitation, and pulmonary HT (all p < 0.05). CKD was associated with increased all-cause mortality (49.3 vs. 26.8%), cardiovascular mortality (28.8 vs. 11.8%), all-cause hospitalizations (47.6 vs. 25.9%), and HF hospitalizations (22.2 vs. 11.0%). Predictors of mortality were LVEF ≤ 40% (Hazard ratio [HR] 1.5, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.1-2.2; p = 0.048), moderate/severe tricuspid regurgitation (HR 1.6, 95% CI 1.1-2.2; p = 0.008), and prior HF hospitalization (HR 2.2, 95% CI 1.6-3.1; p < 0.001). CKD was highly prevalent among patients with HF, particularly among those with LVEF < 50%. Its presence was associated with a more adverse clinical and echocardiographic profile, as well as higher hospitalization, all-cause mortality, and cardiovascular mortality. La coexistencia de insuficiencia cardiaca (IC) y enfermedad renal crónica (ERC) ha sido poco estudiada en Ecuador. El objetivo fue estimar la prevalencia de ERC en pacientes con IC y su impacto pronóstico según la fracción de eyección del ventrículo izquierdo (FEVI). Estudio retrospectivo de un registro unicéntrico ecuatoriano. Se definió la ERC como una tasa de filtración glomerular (TFG) < 60 mL/min/1.73 m². La IC se clasificó según la FEVI reducida (IC-FEr, ≤ 40%), levemente reducida (IC-FElr, 41-49%) o preservada (IC-FEp, ≥ 50%). La mediana de seguimiento fue de 2.28 años. Se incluyeron 706 pacientes (edad 69.9 ± 13.3 años, el 31.4% mujeres). El 50.3% presentó TFG ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m², el 33.1% entre 30 y 59 mL/min/1.73 m², y el 16.6% < 30 mL/min/1.73 m². La prevalencia de ERC fue del 57.8% en la IC-FEr, del 41.8% en la IC-FElr y del 53.5% en la IC-FEp (p = 0.003). Los pacientes con ERC eran mayores y con más hipertensión, fibrilación auricular y enfermedad cerebrovascular, NT-proBNP más alto, mayores diámetros diastólicos, menor FEVI y más insuficiencia tricuspídea e hipertensión pulmonar (p < 0.05). La ERC se asoció con mayor mortalidad total (49.3 vs. 26.8%) y de causa cardiovascular (28.8% vs. 11.8%), y con más hospitalizaciones por cualquier causa (47.6 vs. 25.9%) y por IC (22.2 vs. 11.0%). Los predictores de mortalidad fueron la FEVI ≤ 40% (HR: 1.5; IC 95%: 1.1-2.2; p = 0.048), la insuficiencia tricuspídea moderada/grave (HR: 1.6; IC 95%: 1.1-2.2; p = 0.008) y la hospitalización previa por IC (HR: 2.2; IC 95%: 1.6-3.1; p < 0.001). La ERC fue muy prevalente en los pacientes con IC, especialmente con FEVI < 50%, y se asoció con un perfil clínico y ecocardiográfico más adverso, mayor mortalidad y más hospitalizaciones.

items.title: Performance of Diagnostic Criteria for Autoimmune Encephalitis in Patients With Suspected Rapidly Progressive Dementia.
items.abstract: The Graus criteria for possible autoimmune encephalitis (AE) are increasingly used to identify patients most likely to benefit from autoantibody testing and empiric immunotherapy. However, the performance of Graus criteria in patients with suspected rapidly progressive dementia (RPD) is unknown. We aimed to determine the diagnostic performance of the Graus criteria for possible AE in patients with suspected RPD and to identify the factors associated with progression to autoimmune dementia (AiD). In this observational cohort study, patients ≥18 years with suspected RPD were enrolled and evaluated at 2 tertiary care centers (Washington University in St. Louis, MO, and Mayo Clinic Jacksonville, FL) from 2016 to 2024. Clinical data, brain imaging, electroencephalograms, and biofluid measures were reviewed, and consensus diagnoses were assigned by independent reviewers. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of the Graus criteria for possible AE against the consensus diagnosis. Among patients with AE, multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify factors independently associated with progression to AiD. Two hundred sixty-one patients with suspected RPD were enrolled (mean age 61.1 years, 46% female, 83% non-Hispanic White), including 74 patients (28%) with AE. The Graus criteria for possible AE demonstrated 89% sensitivity, 96% specificity, and 94% accuracy for the diagnosis of AE in patients with suspected RPD. Two patients with AE died within 3 months of symptom onset. Cognitive impairment persisted beyond 3 months in 47 of 72 surviving patients with AE (65%), meeting proposed criteria for AiD. In multivariable analysis, older age (odds ratio [OR] 1.4 per decade, 95% CI 1.0-1.9), longer time to initiation of immunomodulatory treatments (OR 1.4 per month, 95% CI 1.1-1.9), and treatment with rituximab (OR 4.3, 95% CI 1.2-15.1) were independently associated with AiD. The Graus criteria for possible AE reliably identified patients with suspected RPD due to AE. In patients with AE, older age, delays in the initiation of immunomodulatory therapies, and rituximab use (a proxy for severe/refractory AE) were independently associated with progression to AiD. These findings apply to patients evaluated at specialized referral centers and warrant confirmation in broader settings. This study provides Class III evidence that the Graus criteria accurately distinguish AE from other causes of RPD.

items.title: Treatment of Recurrent and/or Metastatic Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: CSCO and ASCO Joint Guideline.
items.abstract: To provide evidence-based recommendations on first- and subsequent-line systemic therapy, maintenance therapy, locoregional consolidation, and salvage local therapy for patients with recurrent and/or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). A multidisciplinary Expert Panel convened by CSCO and ASCO reviewed evidence from randomized trials, meta-analyses, systematic reviews, prospective and retrospective studies, and clinical experience. The guideline was informed by a systematic literature review and consensus-based interpretation of efficacy, safety, feasibility, and patient-centered outcomes across scenarios. Outcomes included overall and progression-free survival, response and disease control rates, toxicity, and quality of life. Evidence supports platinum-based chemotherapy plus a programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor as preferred first-line therapy for medically fit patients. Evidence also supports maintenance strategies after disease control, while treatment selection depends on prior treatment, disease extent, patient fitness, resource availability, and preferences. Selected responders may receive locoregional consolidation radiotherapy or oral maintenance chemotherapy. For isolated locoregional recurrence amenable to local therapy, options include salvage surgery and re-irradiation. Chemotherapy plus a PD-1 inhibitor, followed by maintenance PD-1 inhibition for up to 2 years, should be offered first-line to appropriate patients with recurrent and/or metastatic NPC. Chemotherapy alone may be offered when immunotherapy is unsuitable or declined. Selected patients responding to first-line chemotherapy may receive oral maintenance chemotherapy or locoregional consolidation intensity-modulated radiotherapy. Salvage surgery or re-irradiation is recommended for appropriately selected patients with isolated locoregional recurrence. Subsequent-line options include chemotherapy, PD-1 inhibitors, and antibody-drug conjugates. Treatment should be individualized according to disease setting, prior therapy, expected toxicities, availability, local drug approvals, and patient preferences. Early supportive and specialist interdisciplinary palliative care, where available, should accompany active anticancer treatment for advanced, incurable disease.Additional information is available at www.ascopubs.org/topics/asco-guidelines/head-neck-cancer.
items.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology

items.title: Treatment of Stage IB to III Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: CSCO-ASCO Guideline Update.
items.abstract: To update the 2021 CSCO-ASCO guideline on chemotherapy in combination with radiotherapy for the definitive treatment of non-metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), incorporating new evidence on radiotherapy techniques and target-volume de-escalation, chemotherapy regimens and their sequencing, adjuvant therapy, and immunotherapy for patients with stage IB-III disease. A multidisciplinary Expert Panel reviewed evidence published since the prior guideline, including randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and relevant prospective and retrospective studies. Outcomes of interest included overall survival, failure-free or progression-free survival, locoregional and distant disease control, acute and late toxicities, and patient-reported quality of life. Recommendations were developed using the ASCO guideline development process and Expert Panel consensus. The updated evidence supports: IMRT with image guidance and MRI-based target delineation as core components of definitive treatment; selected response-adapted target delineation following induction chemotherapy; elective nodal de-escalation in appropriately selected patients; risk-adapted chemotherapy sequencing according to stage and biologic risk; cisplatin-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy; gemcitabine-cisplatin (GP) or docetaxel-cisplatin-fluorouracil (TPF) as preferred induction regimens; and selected adjuvant chemotherapy options, including metronomic capecitabine for patients with higher residual post-chemoradiotherapy risk. Several randomized trials evaluating PD-1 inhibitors have demonstrated improved disease-control outcomes, but overall survival data remain immature. This guideline update provides recommendations on radiotherapy technique, dose, imaging, and target delineation; sequencing of additional chemotherapy with radiotherapy; concurrent chemotherapy options; induction chemotherapy regimens and timing; adjuvant chemotherapy options; and the role of immunotherapy. At present, the Panel makes no recommendation for or against routine addition of immunotherapy to induction-concurrent chemoradiotherapy; applicability of the trial evidence, benefits and harms, local approval and access, and patient preferences should guide individualized decisions.Additional information is available at www.ascopubs.org/topics/asco-guidelines/head-neck-cancer.

items.title: Engineered stem cell-derived CD16-enhanced universal NKT cells improve monoclonal antibody-based cancer immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Monoclonal antibody (mAb)-based therapies have revolutionized cancer treatment; however, their clinical efficacy is often limited by insufficient antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC), tumor antigen escape, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). To overcome these limitations, we developed an allogeneic stem cell-derived invariant natural killer T (NKT) cell platform engineered to express a high-affinity non-cleavable CD16 receptor (CD16HSC-NKT) for broad enhancement of mAb-based immunotherapy. Using a clinically guided differentiation platform, we generated highly pure and scalable CD16HSC-NKT cells exhibiting robust expression of NK receptors, potent cytotoxic machinery, and a Th1-biased cytokine profile. CD16HSC-NKT cells demonstrated potent intrinsic antitumor activity and potently enhanced the efficacy of multiple therapeutic antibodies, including Trastuzumab, Tafasitamab, Rituximab, Daratumumab, and Cusatuzumab, across diverse hematologic and solid tumor models. In vivo, combination therapy induced durable tumor eradication and prolonged survival in xenograft models, outperforming the clinically approved antibody-drug conjugate trastuzumab deruxtecan. Mechanistically, therapeutic antibodies promoted the expansion, persistence, and activation of CD16HSC-NKT cells within tumors. CD16HSC-NKT uniquely remodeled the TME by selectively depleting CD1d-expressing tumor-associated macrophages and myeloid-derived suppressor cells. CD16HSC-NKT cells also exhibited minimal alloreactivity, no graft-versus-host disease, and no detectable systemic toxicity. Collectively, these findings establish CD16HSC-NKT cells as a safe, off-the-shelf cellular platform capable of broadly enhancing monoclonal antibody therapy through sustained ADCC, multimodal tumor targeting, and TME remodeling.

items.title: Prevalence of human papillomavirus and HPV vaccination among cisgender bisexual women: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted infection in the United States, and a primary cause of cervical cancer. Although cervical cancer is largely preventable through HPV vaccination, vaccine coverage remains suboptimal. Research on HPV prevalence and vaccination among cisgender bisexual women is limited and inconsistent. This may be partly due to variation in how bisexuality is defined. Bisexuality may be operationalized based on sexual identity (e.g., self-identification as bisexual) or sexual behavior (e.g., sexual contact with more than one sex or gender), and these differing definitions may capture distinct populations and yield divergent health findings. This paper proposes a protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis to examine whether reported HPV prevalence and vaccination rates among cisgender bisexual women differ based on whether bisexuality is defined by identity or behavior. The protocol is registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251252015) and follows PRISMA-P guidelines. Random-effects meta-analyses will estimate pooled HPV prevalence and vaccination rates by definition type. Findings will clarify how operational definitions shape observed HPV-related outcomes and inform tailored cervical cancer prevention strategies for cisgender bisexual women.

items.title: Pooled prevalence of infectious diseases among first responders in the prehospital setting: A systematic review with meta-analysis by occupation.
items.abstract: First responders often work in unpredictable, uncontrolled environments, where exposure to infected patients and contaminated environments heighten the risk of communicable disease transmission. Their higher infection prevalence compared with the general population has driven the implementation of personal protective equipment, vaccination requirements, safety protocols, and infection prevention education. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to estimate the pooled prevalence of infections among first responders in the prehospital workers including paramedics, emergency medical technicians, patient transport staff, firefighters, police, and police officers. Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science and PUBMED/Medline were systematically searched. Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation, with Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation and back-transformation to the original prevalence scale. Heterogeneity was assessed using I², τ², and 95% prediction intervals. Meta-regression was used to examine potential sources of between-study heterogeneity, and small-study effects and potential publication bias were assessed using funnel plots and Egger's regression test. Risk of bias was investigated using the AXIS tool. Following the initial search, 34,874 articles were identified, of which 88 were full-text screened. Of these, 22 studies representing 19,188 first responders were included in this systematic review. The pooled prevalences of hepatitis B and C were 6.2% (95% CI 4.5%-8.2%) and 1.8% (95% CI 0.9%-2.9%), respectively. Around 4% (95% CI 2.6%- 5.9%) of the first responders had MRSA colonisation. Current or past infection with COVID-19 among non-vaccinated first responders was 13.6% (95% CI 4.8%- 25.9%), which reduced to 7.3% (95% CI 3.6%- 12%) after exclusion of studies with high risk of bias. Of the known study characteristics, geographic region significantly contributed to heterogeneity, explaining 36.7% of between-study variance, p  = 0.039. Infectious disease prevalence varied across pathogens, occupations, and geographical settings among first responders. These findings should be interpreted in light of substantial heterogeneity and limitations in the available evidence but may help inform infection prevention, occupational health policy, vaccination strategies, and future research in first responder services.

items.title: Disruption of the NTCP-EGFR receptor complex as a strategy for selective inhibition of hepatitis B and D virus entry.
items.abstract: Hepatitis B and D virus (HBV, HDV) enter hepatocytes through a coordinated process mediated by a receptor complex consisting of sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP), and host entry cofactors, including epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Here, we established an in vitro assay to evaluate the NTCP-EGFR interaction and identified Oxy229, an oxysterol-based compound that disrupted this molecular interaction. Oxy229 selectively inhibited HBV and HDV infection to HepG2-NTCP cells and primary human hepatocytes. Mechanistic analysis revealed that Oxy229 impaired the relocalization of HBV-NTCP complex from the plasma membrane to intracellular vesicles. Notably, Oxy229 did not compromise the physiological functions of NTCP and EGFR, i.e., bile acid transporter and activation of downstream EGFR signaling pathways including Ras-MAPK and PI3K-Akt pathways, indicating selective inhibition of viral entry. Compound derivative analysis identified Oxy283, which acquired dual inhibitory activity against both NTCP-EGFR interaction and NTCP multimerization, resulting in enhanced anti-HBV potency. These findings establish the functional significance of NTCP-receptor complex formation in the HBV/HDV entry and highlight this machinery as a potential target for antiviral intervention.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

items.title: Assessment of physiological changes and levels of KIM-1 and MDA biomarkers resulting from TDM on vancomycin-induced subclinical nephrotoxicity for pediatrics in Al-Najaf city: A casecontrol study.
items.abstract: Aim: The present investigation set out to evaluate the physiological alterations together with the concentrations of the KIM-1 and MDA biomarkers as they relate to TDM-guided Vancomycin treatment. Materials and Methods: A prospective case-control study was undertaken at Al-Zahraa Teaching Hospital, Al-Najaf, Iraq, recruiting 140 pediatric patients receiving intravenous Vancomycin. Through random allocation, participants entered either a control arm administered conventional empirical doses n=70 or a case arm in which dosing was refined by means of pharmacist-led TDM guidance (n=70). Results: The institution of pharmacist-led therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) markedly enhanced attainment of Vancomycin targets and promoted clinical recovery. Within the optimized-therapy group, KIM-1 concentrations declined substantially-signaling diminished renal tubular injury-whereas in those maintained on empirical therapy, these concentrations climbed. TDM-directed dose modifications further yielded a pronounced fall in MDA levels, denoting attenuated oxidative stress. Conclusions: Pharmacist-led therapeutic drug monitoring bolsters both the safety and the efficacy of Vancomycin treatment in the pediatric setting. Calibrating the dose on the strength of TDM translated into superior clinical outcomes while restraining subclinical nephrotoxicity and oxidative stress, as evidenced by the pronounced decline in KIM-1 and MDA concentrations.

items.title: Peripheral blood inflammatory indices may predict distinct serologic patterns of hepatitis B virus infection: a large hospital cohort study.
items.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major public health burden. This study evaluated hematologic characteristics across different serologically defined HBV patterns among hospital attendees in southwest China. A total of 5828 individuals were included in the study. Individuals were classified into 5 study-defined serologic patterns: hepatitis B surface antigen positive (HBsAg+)/hepatitis B e antigen positive (HBeAg+) (active replication stage), HBsAg+/hepatitis B e antibody positive (HBeAb+) (immune control stage), HBsAg+/HBeAg-/HBeAb- (transition infection stage), isolated anti-hepatitis B core (HBc), and anti-HBc+/anti-HBs+ (resolved infection stage), according to qualitative HBV serology. These descriptive patterns are not validated clinical infection phases. The overall HBsAg seropositivity rate was approximately 3%. HBsAg positivity was more frequent in male individuals (odds ratio, 1.26), whereas the odds of HBsAg positivity were lower in participants younger than 24 years of age (odds ratio, 0.33). Neural network models showed moderate ability to discriminate immune states using complete blood cell count-derived indices (area under the curve = 0.721). Nevertheless, the lymphocyte to monocyte ratio and systemic inflammation response index revealed a substantial trend from innate immune activation in active replication/transition infection stage to adaptive immune predominance in immune control/resolved infection stage. The isolated anti-HBc pattern was characterized by a reduced eosinophil to lymphocyte ratio, although this association is descriptive and does not establish occult infection or immune surveillance. Complete blood cell count-derived inflammatory indices were associated with different serologic HBV patterns. More evidence of immune transition or progressive immune remodeling is required, however.

items.title: Technetium-99m-labeled HBsAg-conjugated anionic linear-globular dendrimers: radiolabeling and preclinical biodistribution.
items.abstract: Radiolabeling of nanocarriers can facilitate preclinical evaluation of their biodistribution and organ accumulation in healthy mice. HBsAg was conjugated to G2-ALGD using carbodiimide chemistry and subsequently radiolabeled with technetium-99m (D-HBsAg-⁹⁹ᵐTc). The resulting nanoplatform was characterized in terms of its physicochemical properties, radiochemical purity, and preliminary cytocompatibility. Its in vivo biodistribution was evaluated in BALB/c mice using single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) imaging and ex vivo radiometry. D-HBsAg-⁹⁹ᵐTc nanotracers were 148.3 ± 24.5 nm in size and showed a zeta potential of + 3.65 mV. FTIR verified amide bond formation at 1649 cm⁻¹ between the dendrimer's carboxyl groups and HBsAg's amino groups. They showed no significant cytotoxicity in HFF-2 cells up to 100 µg/mL after 24 h. These nanoconjugates achieved a radiochemical purity of 95.83% and remained radiochemically stable for 24 h without detectable technetium leakage. Ex vivo biodistribution and SPECT imaging demonstrated significantly greater hepatic accumulation of D-HBsAg-⁹⁹ᵐTc than free ⁹⁹ᵐTc (22.89 ± 0.45 vs. 0.88 ± 0.42%ID/g, P < 0.05). Compared with HBsAg-⁹⁹ᵐTc, D-HBsAg-⁹⁹ᵐTc exhibited comparable liver uptake (22.89 ± 0.45 vs. 20.78 ± 4.23%ID/g) but substantially lower splenic (6.34 ± 0.21 vs. 11.66 ± 0.28%ID/g) and gastrointestinal accumulation, indicating improved hepatic accumulation and reduced off-target distribution. This nanoplatform represents a promising technetium-99m-labeled nano-tracer and demonstrated preferential hepatic accumulation in healthy mice, supporting its feasibility for preclinical biodistribution studies. Future studies should evaluate its immunogenicity and antiviral activity in appropriate HBV animal models to determine whether it may have applications beyond preclinical biodistribution imaging.
items.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences

items.title: Temporal Dosing Tunes Glutathione Gradient across Liver-Blood-Tumor Axes to Boost the Chemotherapeutic Potency of Prodrug Nanoassemblies.
items.abstract: Redox-responsive prodrug nanodelivery systems hold immense promise in cancer therapy, offering advantages of improved pharmacokinetics, enhanced tumor selectivity, and increased safety. However, compared with standard therapeutic formulations, prodrug nanodelivery systems fail to yield superior antitumor efficacy at equivalent doses, attributable to inadequate drug activation and intratumoral accumulation. Herein, the three-in-one drug-release module, comprising an α-disulfide bond, an ethylene glycol moiety, and a short carbon chain, was covalently linked to paclitaxel (PTX) to construct three prodrug nanoassemblies (PSBA10 NPs, PSBA12 NPs, PSBA14 NPs). Notably, PSBA10 NPs, which possessed the shortest carbon chain, exhibited hypersensitive redox-responsive drug release and potentiated antitumor efficacy. Although PSBA10 NPs exhibited better safety than paclitaxel solution (Taxol) at equivalent doses, superior efficacy remained unattainable. Interestingly, a temporal-dose-regulated glutathione (GSH) gradient across the liver-blood-tumor axis increased the intratumoral accumulation of PSBA10 NPs by approximately 3-fold, resulting in pronounced antitumor efficacy superior to Taxol. This transient depletion of GSH in the liver and blood reduced the cleavage of disulfide bonds in the systemic circulation, enhancing tumor accumulation and selective activation of PSBA10 NPs. Our study highlighted a tumor treatment model based on the synergistic strategy of structural optimization and GSH gradient regulation across the liver-blood-tumor axis to boost the efficacy of chemotherapy.

items.title: Nanoscale Immune Activator for Enhancing CD8+ T Cell Infiltration in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
items.abstract: The infiltration of CD8+ T cells into the hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) microenvironment is a well-established determinant of immunotherapy efficacy and patient prognosis. However, the regulatory mechanisms governing this process and the therapeutic strategies capable of modulating it remain largely unexplored. Here, we identify HCC-IN-247 as a candidate compound that enhances IFNβ-driven CD8+ T cell infiltration both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the long noncoding RNA LINC02084 directly interacts with the transcription factor GLIS1 and facilitates its recruitment to the IFNβ promoter. HCC-IN-247 was identified through screening to target the LINC02084-GLIS1 binding interface, thereby stabilizing this RNA-protein complex. Stabilization of the complex significantly enhances IFNβ transcription, which in turn upregulates CXCL10 and CXCL11 expression and promotes CD8+ T cell infiltration. Furthermore, this study engineered a nanoparticle-based delivery system, designated Lip@RA@BSA-PD-L1/IN-247, for the codelivery of HCC-IN-247 and the anti-PD-L1 antibody atezolizumab in HCC treatment. These nanoparticles exhibited robust tumor-specific accumulation and elicited potent synergistic antitumor activity against HCC in mice. Collectively, our findings establish HCC-IN-247 as an activator of the tumor immune microenvironment and provide a preclinical basis for a combined immunotherapeutic approach to HCC.

items.title: Metformin sensitizes HepG2 liver cancer cells to doxorubicin through epithelial to mesenchymal transition and microRNA regulation.
items.abstract: Although therapeutic strategies have improved, liver cancer continues to impose a major global disease burden, largely due to its aggressive metastatic behavior and limited responsiveness to conventional chemotherapy. Metformin, a widely prescribed anti-diabetic drug, has shown emerging anti-tumor potential; however, its mechanisms, particularly in combination with chemotherapeutic agents, are not fully elucidated. This study explores the combined effects of metformin and the standard chemotherapeutic agent doxorubicin on the suppression of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), an essential driver of metastasis and chemoresistance, in HepG2 liver cancer cells. Low-dose combination treatment, optimized by SRB assay, markedly enhanced their antiproliferative activity compared with either drug alone. Consistently, wound-healing assays showed that the combined therapy more effectively inhibited HepG2 cell wound closure, suggesting a potential inhibitory effect on cell motility. Furthermore, the combined therapy altered EMT markers: upregulating epithelial markers (E-cadherin and Integrin-α5) while repressing mesenchymal markers Vimentin. These changes were accompanied by repression of key EMT-inducing transcription factors, including ZEB1, SNAIL1 and SNAIL2. Furthermore, qPCR analysis revealed that the combination significantly altered the expression of several EMT-associated miRNAs, including miR-215-5p, miR-122-5p, miR-429, miR-200c-3p, and miR-138-3p, with a strong upregulation of the miR-200 family, the classical EMT regulators. In conclusion, our findings show that metformin possesses anti-cancer effects that are significantly amplified when combined with doxorubicin. This combined treatment targeting the EMT pathway, offers a promising strategy to suppress metastasis and chemoresistance and improve therapeutic outcomes in liver cancer.

items.title: The mechanism of METTL6/DALRD3 regulating cell cycle-mediated chemoresistance in hepatocellular carcinoma.
items.abstract: Chemoresistance worsens the prognosis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study focuses on how methyltransferase-like protein 6 (METTL6)/DALR anticodon binding domain containing 3 (DALRD3) regulates cell cycle progression and impacts HCC chemoresistance. HCC cell lines with relatively low or high METTL6 expression were intervened with cisplatin (DDP) to construct DDP-resistant cell models, and later transfected with overexpression (oe)-METTL6 plasmid, oe-DALRD3 plasmid, small interfering RNA (si)-METTL6, and/or si-DALRD3. A battery of cellular biological functional experiments and DDP drug sensitivity tests were performed to characterize the modulatory effects of METTL6 or DALRD3 on HCC chemoresistance. The interaction between METTL6 and DALRD3 was validated using coimmunoprecipitation. 3-methylcytosine (m 3 C) modification and expression were further detected using dot blot and Northern blot assays. A subcutaneous xenograft mouse model was established with METTL6- or DALRD3-deficient HCC cells, which were exposed to DDP for experimental validation of in vitro findings. METTL6 and DALRD3 were upregulated in DDP-resistant HCC cells, and their upregulation in HCC tissues correlated with poor prognosis. Re-expression of METTL6 or DALRD3 led to strengthened cell proliferation, aggravated cell cycle progression, and augmented DDP chemoresistance. The validated METTL6-DALRD3 interaction increased m 3 C modification. Northern blot further validated serine transfer RNA-m 3 C at position 32 (tRNA Ser -m 3 C32) modification mediated by the METTL6-DALRD3 complex. Rescue experiments unveiled that DALRD3 overexpression reversed METTL6 knockdown-mediated HCC phenotypes. Either METTL6 or DALRD3 knockdown potentiated DDP chemosensitivity in HCC xenograft mice. METTL6/DALRD3 mediated tRNA Ser -m 3 C32 modification may participate in DDP resistance in HCC cells by regulating cell cycle progression.

items.title: Ceramide-mediated immunometabolic modulation in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC): emerging functions of sphingomyelin phosphodiesterase 3 (SMPD3).
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) develops within a metabolically constrained and immunologically heterogeneous tumor microenvironment in which malignant, stromal, and immune cells compete for nutrients and exchange bioactive metabolites. Ceramide is a main sphingolipid intermediate and signaling lipid with several biological effects, which depend on acyl-chain composition, subcellular localization, metabolic flux, and cellular context. Sphingomyelin phosphodiesterase 3 (SMPD3), also known as neutral sphingomyelinase 2 (nSMase2), generates ceramide through sphingomyelin hydrolysis and also participates in extracellular-vesicle biogenesis. HCC-specific findings claimed that reduced SMPD3 expression could be associated with adverse clinicopathological features and suppression of malignant phenotypes after SMPD3 restoration, could be in favor of a tumor-restraining function. However, direct evidence that endogenous SMPD3-derived ceramide reprograms the metabolism of infiltrating immune cells in primary HCC is currently lacking. This review distinguishes HCC-specific findings from mechanistic evidence derived from tumor and inflammatory systems. We integrate ceramide biosynthesis and turnover, HCC immunometabolism, T-cell and myeloid-cell metabolic states, extracellular-vesicle communication, and therapeutic studies using ceramide nanoliposomes. We also discuss the context-dependent relationship between ceramide and apoptosis, autophagy, mitochondrial dysfunction, and ferroptosis, emphasizing that endogenous SMPD3-derived ceramide and exogenous short-chain ceramide formulations are not biologically interchangeable. Finally, we define experimental priorities required to test cell-specific SMPD3 functions, resolve ceramide species and spatial flux, validate biomarkers, and determine whether selective restoration of the SMPD3-ceramide axis can improve immunotherapy or other systemic treatment strategies in HCC.
